summary: David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey.

David Zilberman (1938–1977) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied under Yuri Levada (1968–1972). He held posts at Odesa University, Hunter College, the University of Chicago, and Brandeis University.

Davoud Monchi-Zadeh (1914–1989) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Walther Wüst, later holding academic positions at the University of Munich, Alexandria University, and Uppsala University.
Daw Ohn (1913–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics. She studied at the University of Rangoon, where she also served as Tutor in Pali (attested 1977).

Dawa Norbu (1949–2006) specialized in Tibetology and history. He studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and UC Berkeley, and served as Professor of Central Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1984–2004).
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He has held a post at Tibet University.
Dawei Wang specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sichuan University and held an appointment at its Institute for Daoism and Religious Culture Studies.

Daya Krishna (1924–2007) was a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor of philosophy and Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1961–1984) and chaired the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni (1879–1939) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Oriental College and the University of the Punjab under John Marshall. He held posts with the Archaeological Survey of India and Jaipur State.

Dayananda Saraswati (1824–1883) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Sri Jayachamarajendra Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and under teachers including Virajanand Dandeesha, P. S. Subramania Iyer, Veeraraghavachariar, Swami Pranavananda, Swami Tarananda Giri, and Swami Tapovan Maharaj.

Dayong (1893–1929) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute—where he taught in 1923—and under teachers including Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Bai Puren, and Dorje Geshe.

Debala Mitra (1925–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.
Debamitra Dey is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She completed both her BA Honours in Sanskrit (1997–2000) and her PhD (2003–2008) at Jadavpur University.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cornell University. He founded and directed the Central Institute of Indian Languages (~1969–1989) and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata, and was a visiting professor at the University of Calcutta.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian and Tibetologist who earned her PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar and completed her Habilitation at the University of Vienna, where she held the chair for Asian art history (1994–2015).

Deborah Sutton is a historian and Indologist who earned her PhD in modern history from Jawaharlal Nehru University (1997–2001). She serves as Professor in Modern South Asian History at Lancaster University (attested 2026).
Declan Quigley is an Indologist who has held teaching positions at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei (born 1968) is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998), where he became associate professor of religious studies around 2002.

Deepro Chakraborty is an Indologist who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Alberta (PhD 2017). He has held academic posts at St. Stephen's College, Gurudas College, and the University of Alberta.
